summary: Subject and prompt held at their dispatched digests, both read-only. Every attack axis fails. The one that had teeth is the DR-009 rider, because I raised the advisory it answers and could therefore check whether the answer is honest: it is. The rider's only new content is a path and a digest, and that digest matches live bytes exactly; every semantic sentence in it — not park closure, not SATISFIED, LN-13 and derivationDigest and R1-PARK-* and CIR-B1 still open — is already present in the v2 artifact it rides on. So it is the pin, not a new claim. All fifteen cited digests match, including my own three verdicts and their recited counts, and both commits resolve.
whatIVerified: Prompt digest at start and end: adcf56525bae85fa7e641b0cdd6184b8abb2b3874a135e08523fa1b0b5bab00b, equal to the dispatch-supplied value. Subject at 7da3adf88694b3f8232801206bb424ada99409a725fdbd62172406b990128e02, equal to both the dispatch and the prompt. Three measurements each at start and again at end; both -r--r--r-- at both ends.

The attack 'rider RB-DR009-V2-A1 is a new semantic claim rather than the pin' fails, and I could test this unusually well because RBDR009V2-C2-A1 is my own advisory. The rider reads: 'the applied lineage head named by v2 is docs/coop/artifacts/r1-lifetime-neutrality.conformance.v1.9.json 37897be0cca011e88c04b93b6f9912f444006b4b3c71e99a08b253d613c9c0ab. Application of that head is still not park closure and is still not SATISFIED. The rider answers Claude 2 advisory RBDR009V2-C2-A1 (pin missing). It does not close LN-13, derivationDigest, R1-PARK-*, or CIR-B1.' I checked each semantic element against the v2 artifact: 'not park closure', 'not SATISFIED of this row', and the open standing of LN-13, policyOutcome.derivationDigest, R1-PARK-* and CIR-B1 are all already in v2. The only content the rider adds is the path and the digest — exactly what my advisory asked for and nothing else.

The rider's pin is correct, which is the check that mattered most: a rider that supplied a wrong digest would be worse than the omission it repairs. docs/coop/artifacts/r1-lifetime-neutrality.conformance.v1.9.json measures 37897be0cca011e88c04b93b6f9912f444006b4b3c71e99a08b253d613c9c0ab against live bytes, identical to the pinned value.

The rider is carried into the owner-recording obligation rather than left decorative: D-076 clause 2 states 'The disposition owners must record is v2 plus this rider', and clause 3 states 'Condition 1 does not discharge until the owner records v2 plus the rider.' D-076's subject line is correspondingly 'route-b.DR-009.preview-disposition.v2.json plus the rider in clause 2', which is why it does not use the word 'only' that D-074 and D-075 use — that difference is correct, not an inconsistency.

The route chosen instead of a v3 is disclosed and precedented. The rejected alternative reads 'Write a v3 just to add the digest and re-review. Rejected for this cycle: the advisory is pin discipline, not a semantic defect; D-039 already recorded an ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES disposition plus an operative rider.' That characterisation of my advisory is faithful — I wrote that it was 'not about the decision at all' and classified it as pin discipline — and the precedent holds: adopted D-039 reads 'The disposition owners must record is v2 plus this rider (RB-DR005-V2-A1)' and uses the same sentence D-076 uses, 'An ACCEPT or ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES verdict is not owner recording.'

The attack 'cited verdicts are not ACCEPT / ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES 0 blockers' fails, and the three rows describing my verdicts are exact because I wrote those files. DR-006 Claude 2 at d1f30920… is ACCEPT with 0 blockers and 0 advisories; DR-007 at aa70e150… is ACCEPT 0/0; DR-009 at b4c59368… is ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES, 0 blockers, 1 advisory, and its id is RBDR009V2-C2-A1 — matching the recital character for character.

All fifteen cited digests match live bytes: the three v2 dispositions (28fb23ec…, 53b72a91…, 5e2f6572…, the same values I measured at both ends of my own review of them), my three verdicts, the three Codex verdicts (821ce53f…, 807d0b63…, 2401819f…, hashed without opening), the r1 v1.9 head, COORD ad6e24b2…, and file 08 9495c70f….

The attack 'treats ACCEPT as owner recording' fails in every entry. 'is not owner recording' appears six times across the file — each entry carries both 'This is not owner recording' and 'An ACCEPT verdict is not owner recording', with D-076 correctly widening its second to 'An ACCEPT or ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES verdict is not owner recording'. Each entry also names the owner who must record and states the disposition is the accepted draft, not the record. The alternatives sections reject the conflation by name.

The attack 'silent SATISFIED or condition-1 discharge' fails per entry rather than only in the header. Each of the three states its row 'stays HARD-BLOCKED' — which I confirmed against file 08, where DR-006, DR-007 and DR-009 all lead HARD-BLOCKED — and each states condition 1 does not discharge until the owner records, with 'Conditions 2–5 remain' and 'Condition 5 remains the only implementation authorization' appearing three times. Every readiness effect is 'Zero.'

The attack 'records v1 citing CONTESTED D-051-053' fails: each entry records the v2 artifact by name and digest and attributes the authorization to the adopted new-cycle selection, and D-074's alternatives reject the error explicitly — 'Record v1 citing CONTESTED D-051. Rejected: D-069 is the adopted selection.' D-069, D-071 and D-072 are all present in COORD and ADOPTED.

The attack 'treats r1 v1.9 as park closure' fails: the rider states application is 'still not park closure and is still not SATISFIED', the alternatives reject 'Treat applied r1 v1.9 as SATISFIED of the parks', and clause 3 leaves the parks and a reviewed retained validator owed.

The attack 'treats D-073 as still in-flight or overturns it' fails: the preamble states D-073 is ADOPTED at f0c99ef739d63e4164d1e79ba712cc7140c6356c, which resolves to 'D-073: correct D-069 Codex verdict digest', that it 'does not reopen those selections', and that 'This file does not adopt or overturn D-073.' COORD confirms D-073 present and ADOPTED.

The attacks 'condition 5 / docs/v2/implementation' and 'file 08 edited' fail: the header refuses to authorize docs/v2/implementation/, each entry preserves condition 5 as the only implementation authorization, 'Does not edit file 08 (MF-6)' appears three times, file 08 measures unchanged at its cited digest, and git reports zero modified tracked files.

Severability is real rather than asserted. Each entry declares its own single subject, states 'adopting or overturning this entry does not change' the other two by name, and carries its own Decision, Alternatives, Readiness effect and Reversibility with a distinct overturn code — C-D074, C-D075, C-D076. Each would stand alone if severed.
The form citation is accurate: D-039, D-040, D-041, D-049 and D-050 are all present in COORD, all ADOPTED, and all are recordings of preview Route B dispositions — the same instrument class.
I wrote one file, the verdict named for me, and edited and committed nothing.

The merits of the three v2 dispositions beyond my separate reviews of them, whose stated limits I carry forward, including that I did not audit freeze §7.1's identity-recipe property, the contents of d9-exit-contract.v1.14, or the substance of LN-13, derivationDigest, R1-PARK-* and CIR-B1.

consentNote: I CONSENT on all three entries with zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX. The axis worth dwelling on is the DR-009 rider, because it answers an advisory I raised and I was therefore in a position to check whether the answer was real or cosmetic. It is real: the pinned digest matches live bytes, and every sentence in the rider other than the pin is a restatement of something v2 already says — so it discharges the advisory without smuggling in a new claim, which is exactly the failure mode the dispatch names. The choice to carry it as a rider rather than reissue a v3 is disclosed, follows adopted D-039, and rests on a characterisation of my advisory as pin discipline that matches what I actually wrote. All three of my verdict recitals are exact, and each entry stands alone with its own subject, alternatives, readiness effect and overturn code.
